WHO WE ARE

Our compassionate staff is committed to serving you in your time of need. We will do everything in our power to make your experience meaningful and memorable, and each family is treated the way we would want our families to be treated.
OUR FACILITY

Our funeral home offers a warm, comfortable, family-oriented environment with traditional architecture and tasteful interior decor. Our facilities accommodate all types of funerals and memorials large and small, public or private.
SERVICES WE OFFER

We offer personalized, professional, and compassionate services to you and your family. Our goal is to lessen the burden on your family so that you can focus on celebrating your loved one's life and beginning your grief journey towards healing.

“ Benta's is a long established business that my family has known of for years so when my father passed after a long illness, my sister and decided that this would be the best place to handle the arrangements. My father passed during a holiday weekend (July 4th) so we had to wait until the next day to start final arrangements but the funeral director that was assigned to us Chontel Harris was great. We told her our budget and she was understanding telling us the options without additional pressure to add extras. She explained the process in detail from that day to the day of the funeral; communication was easy and prompt. In the end my sister and I were satisfied with the service provided by Benta's Funeral Home”
— Elleanora B. Bloomfield, NJ

“Dean Wilson - what an incredible human being. From the moment we met, he made my family and I feel at ease. This is a difficult, confusing, and very overwhelming process, but Dean made it all feel so effortless. Benta was recommended to us by the pastor of Our Lady of Lourdes Church and I have zero regrets. Dean went the extra mile for us, making a stop at my mother's building during the funeral procession to leave flowers at the front steps. Incredible. A simple gesture that will forever stay embedded in my memory and our hearts. I know the other reviews make this place seem like a nightmare and it worried me at first, too. Dean and his team at Benta made all those fears vanish. They took great attention to all the details, even the smallest ones were not overlooked. Mom looked dashing in her casket. I would 100% recommend Benta to family and friends.”

/our-history.title: Our History — Benta's Funeral Home, Inc.
paragraphs: Harlem is known internationally as the Black Mecca of the world, but Harlem has been home to many races and ethnic groups including the Dutch, Irish, German, Italian, and Jewish. Harlem was originally settled by the Dutch in 1658, but was largely farmland and undeveloped territory for approximately 200 years. As New York’s population grew, residential and commercial expansion moved northward, and development of the Harlem territory was inevitable.

Benta's Funeral Home has been servicing families continuously since 1928. We are there when you need us. We understand the needs and traditions of our friends and neighbors. Our professional funeral directors and staff are available to help you through all phases of arrangement. We have private counseling and pre-need services available.

In 1928, George A. Benta recognized a need in the Harlem Community and in a small way, he tried to fulfill it. Although he was hampered in many ways because of economic circumstances, he possessed a strong respect and sense of brotherhood for the members of his community. Always motivated by this respect and brotherhood, he committed himself to conduct his business with a quality of service which would be unrivaled. Together with his wife, Helena M. Benta, a licensed funeral director, who died in 1951, Mr. Benta led the Benta Funeral Home through 38 years of continuous growth, until his death in 1966.

Continuing the tradition of quality service, his successor, George B. Benta . He assumed the weighty reins of ownership and was responsible for ensuring that Benta’s Funeral Home continued stellar reputation with quality and service being their number one priority. He remained current in the funeral industry and Chair Emeritus until his passing in 2013.

Celebrating over 97 years of service to the community, the next generation of Benta’s has taken helm. George Jason A. Benta, the great-grandson of George A., works to differentiate his family’s business from all new comers as well as the old ways. Jason Benta has invested in the future by adding new technology and advanced systems while honoring the traditions of his family’s beloved funeral industry.

paragraphs: Based on the General Price List that each funeral home is required to display, Benta's Funeral Home service charges are among the most affordable.
Yes, continuously since 1928.

Cremation is much less expensive than an earth burial. But it also depends on the type of services that a family selects. Direct cremation is the least expensive of all services with no family involvement.
Depending on the family's needs, a funeral arrangement can take anywhere from one hour to two hours.
Funeral services are usually scheduled from 3 - 7 days after the person passes away. Once the person is embalmed, the remains are well preserved until the day of the funeral service.

Pre-arranged funerals are for the sole comfort that one's funeral wishes will be carried out. It saves the bereaved family a lot of guesswork as to what the deceased may have wanted. People of all ages have established pre-arranged funerals with the funeral home.

As we have no control over the rising costs of cemeteries, vendors, etc., we are only able to guarantee the cost of the casket as quoted on the day of the pre-arrangement with a deposit of $500.00 to activate this interest bearing account.

Yes, provided it is a revocable pre-arrangement, you are entitled to a refund or transfer to another funeral home of your choice. If it is an irrevocable pre-arrangement (Medicaid recipient), monies are not refundable but are transferable.
Fortunately, prepayments are accepted only for pre-arranged funerals. Unfortunately, once a death occurs all payments must be made 48 hours prior to the funeral service taking place.
Floral arrangements can be sent to either the funeral home or the church. Please allow the florist ample time to ensure your delivery is timely.

JSharon Odette Allen  passed away from a cardiovascular blockage at the age of 71 in Lincoln Hospital in the Bronx, New York on Friday, September 11, 2026.

Sharon, affectionately known as “Buckwheat” or simply “Buck” by family and friends, was born on July 17, 1955 in New York to Alphonso Allen and Shirley Jones-Allen. She worked hard to help others and to be an inspiration to her family, friends, and patients. She was a faith warrior who believed in God with all her heart, mind, and spirit. Her strong faith gave her the strength and the passion to inspire, help, and care for others even while she was in pain.

James “J.C.” Coleman Fields was born on June 19, 1934, in Farmerville, Louisiana, to Alter Mae Jones-Fields and Horace “Hoy” Fields. He was the second-born of six children and was raised in Farmerville, where he attended the local school system before migrating to Harlem, New York.  He then attended Cooper High School here in Manhattan NY.

In the mid 1940s, James joined his parents and family in Harlem after they had moved north in search of a stable and promising future for their children. He went on to build a life marked by hard work, dedication, and perseverance.
Dorothy Nicholas Evans, 97, of Palm Coast, Florida, was born on May 3, 1929 and left us to be with the Master Caregiver on August 25, 2026.

She was a graduate of George Washington High School, Lincoln School for Nurses and Marymount College, where she received a Bachelor of Science degree. She was married to Waymon Evans andhad a long career as a healthcare professional in New York before moving to Palm Coast to enjoy her retirement.
A lifelong learner, she enjoyed reading and traveling.
Sean Anthony Diaz, Sr.  was born in New York, New York, to the proud parents Margaret Prosser-Williams and William Diaz on September 9, 1967. He was the eldest child of the family.

Sean spent his childhood and teenage years in New York City, where he attended elementary, middle, and high school in Manhattan. He graduated from Murray Bergtraum High School and later moved to Dallas, Texas, to pursue his studies at DeVry.

Jean “Gigi” Goldsmith peacefully departed this earthly life on August 4, 2026 leaving behind a remarkable legacy of grace, dignity, strength, service, and unwavering love. Just seventeen days shy of her ninety-ninth birthday, Jean had lived through nearly a century of extraordinary change, meeting each season of life with determination, intelligence, elegance, and an abiding devotion to family.
Born Lillie Jean Hallums on August 21, 1927, in Greenville, South Carolina, Jean was the daughter of Caroline Leland Hallums and James Arthur Hallums.

Marie Virginie Land  was born on March 4, 1931, in Bainet, Haiti, to Lormilus Land and Cherizane Marcelin. She was known throughout her life by her middle name, Virginie, the name by which her family, friends, and community knew and loved her.

Virginie married Anoal Abricak Gedeon and began building her family in Haiti. Their children included daughters Geordana, Elna, and Pauline, and sons Peguerot and his twin brother. Virginie experienced the heartbreaking loss of two of her children early in life: Peguerot’s twin brother, who passed away shortly after birth, and Pauline, who passed away as a young child.

Lerlean Taborn  was born on December 2, 1923, to the late Irvin Burnside and Sarah (Ware) Burnside. Lerlean Taborn was the fourth of 11 children, all of whom preceded Lerlean in death. Lerlean Taborn was born in Greenville, South Carolina, in Simpsonville County. She departed this life into the arms of her loving Savior on July 16, 2026, at 6:45 am in New York City.
Lerlean’s early childhood was spent in Simpsonville, South Carolina. At the age of 6, her parents moved to Detroit, Michigan.

Alicia Elizabeth George was born in New York to loving parents Lillian McBean and Rudolph George. She was the sixth of seven children; she was raised in a close-knit family which instilled the values of hard work, kindness and dedication. She attended Mable Dean Beacon High School then continued her education at Borough of Manhattan Community College where she graduated with a degree in Business Administration.
Following her graduating she began her remarkable career servicing the 23rd precinct where she briefly worked as a 911 operator before she transitioned into a secretarial administrative role.

We gather today to celebrate a life that taught us how to be steady, curious, and kind. Thurmond Edward Smalls was a man of quiet strength — the kind of person whose presence made ordinary days feel important. He did not seek the spotlight, but he left a light behind him that will guide us for years to come.

Thurmond was born on Pawleys Island, South Carolina, the seventh of eight children of Ethel and James Smalls. From that large, loving household he carried forward a deep sense of family and responsibility.

Rachel Martha Northcross was born on September 7, 1923, in Beaufort County, South Carolina, to the late Nathan and Rosetta J. Simmons. She moved to New York City as an adult to build a new life. In December of 1951, she was united in holy matrimony to her husband, Johnny Northcross. For most of her life, Rachel worked in New York’s historic garment industry as a skilled seamstress, using her hands and creativity to provide for her family. Her spirit of service did not stop at retirement. She continued to work part-time for many years as a certified home attendant, bringing comfort, dignity, and care to those who needed it most.

JoAnn Harris Johnson passed away unexpectedly in Harlem, NYC on June 30, 2026. JoAnn was born at Columbia Presbyterian Hospital in Upper Manhattan on October 1, 1944, the second child of her loving parents, Robert C. Harris Sr. of Caroline County, Virginia, and Mary Louise Harris, née Hobson, of Powhatan, Virginia. She attended Resurrection Elementary School for eight years and then George Washington High School, graduating with honors. She also attended City College. JoAnn worked at General Vision for several decades, where she was a shop steward, before retiring. A devoted Catholic with a loving and sociable spirit, JoAnn was kind to everyone around her. She was often cracking jokes and didn’t put up with any nonsense.
Carolyn Cardwell passed away peacefully on June 22, 2026, in a manner that reflected the way she lived her life; on her own terms.

In accordance with her wishes, there will be no funeral or memorial service. Instead, she hoped her life would be remembered not through a single gathering, but through the lives she touched and the values she cherished.
We honor Carolyn by embracing life's joys and challenges with grace, giving thanks to God, and remaining ever grateful for the gift of family, friendship, and each day we are given.

Lafielia Iesha Fields was born on September 1, 1987, in Harlem, New York, toWilhelmina Perkins and John Victor Fields. From the start, Lafielia was a surprise blessing — a bright light who brought instant joy to her parents and siblings. One of her earliest acts of love was helping our family move from Harlem to the Bronx. To us, that was no small thing. It was an enormous feat, and she led it with determination and heart.

Lafielia had a will that wouldn’t quit. Despite reading challenges, she proudly graduated from Martin Luther King Jr. Law and Justice High School. Her dream of higher education never faded. She attended Briarcliffe College, Monroe College, University of Phoenix, and others, always reaching for that degree.

Margaret Geneva Hubbard (McCoy) was born in Harlem, New York, on February 8, 1932, to the proud parents Russell McCoy and Mable Godwin McCoy. From the very beginning, Margaret’s life was marked by warmth, grace, and a deep love for family.

Margaret was educated through the New York City school system, having graduated from Washington Irving High School before pursuing a professional education in stenography. As a young girl, she nurtured her love for the arts through ballet and tap dance classes, cherishing the memories of her recitals.
Carol Taylor departed this life on May 4, 2026, surrounded by the love of family and friends. She will be remembered for her warmth, kindness, strength, and the joy she brought to all who knew her.

Born on July 29, 1947, in Manhattan, New York, Carol lived a life rooted in love, family, friendship, education, and community. She was known for her beautiful spirit, caring heart, and her remarkable ability to make others feel welcomed, valued, and encouraged.
After an extremely short battle with sickness, Patricia Ann Scarborough  passed away peacefully on Monday, April 13, 2026.

Born in Bishopville, South Carolina on July 25, 1954, Patricia moved to New York as a young child. She received her formal education in South Carolina school system. After graduating from high school, Patricia attended City College and graduated with a Bachelor’s degree in Sociology.
Patricia was a faithful member of Saint Catherine’s of Genoa Church, New York, NY for 25 years or more, and served in many capacities.

Melvin Phillip (aka Brim), son of Daniel Phillip and Esther Phillip-Strahan was born on September 7, 1947 in San Juan, Trinidad. He was the father of Melvin, Curtis (deceased) and Tanyshia Phillip, brother of Myrna Worrell, Martin Phillip and many others. The uncle of Hilton Jr., Kevin and Melissa Worrell and had many extended family members. He fell asleep in death on March 30, 2026. Melvin migrated to St. Thomas in 1967 and after he was recruited in the United States Army. He continued his education at Medgar Evers College and received a BA degree and then attended The New School University to obtain a Masters degree.
Loretta M. Acquaah was born on May 12, 1984, at New York Presbyterian Hospital in Manhattan to her loving parents, John M. Acquaah and Comfort Acquaah. She was the youngest of five children.

Loretta began her education at PS 46 Elementary School in Harlem, graduating on June 20, 1994. She continued her academic journey at A. Philip Randolph High School, where she graduated on June 25, 2002. Loretta went on to earn her Bachelor’s degree from John Jay College and later completed her Master of Social Work at Hunter College on June 5, 2009.

Emma Cloyd-Anderson was born November 14, 1946, in Brooklyn, New York, the eldest of three children. She peacefully made her transition on March 6, 2026. She was a Queen among women and possessed insight, discernment, wisdom and grace.

Emma also affectionately called Carolina, attended Maxwell High School in Brooklyn and City College of New York. She had a lifelong passion for assisting children, especially children with Special Needs.  Emma worked at the Board of Education as a Special Education Liaison.  She especially loved helping students with Adult Living Skills training.

Albert Williams was born on February 26, 1962 in Bronx, New York to proud parents Mary Bridges Williams and Collins Williams Sr. Raised in the vibrant Bronx environment. Albert carried the spirit, resilience, and warmth of his community with him throughout his life.

Albert received his early education in the New York City public school system at P.S. 23. Al “Ice-Man” Williams then brought his passion for basketball from the streets to the Franklin School, a private high school now known as Dwight School.

Vanessa Olivia Middleton-Gilchrist age 62, passed away on Friday, February 27, 2026. Affectionately known as “Nessy”, she was born August 29, 1963in New York City, NY to Margaret Clement-Middleton and Herman Middleton of Charleston, South Carolina.

Vanessa was the fourth of six children: Zetta Brown (deceased), Evelyn Robinson, Elaine Lovell (deceased), Herman Middleton Jr., and KevinMiddleton. She is survived by her husband, Eric Gilchrist; her nieces and nephews, Deaver Varner, Andre “Dre” Lovell Jr, Caprice T. McMullen, Tee-Tee Middleton, Tenita Robinson, Celina Messón, & Dominique Middleton and a host of grandnieces and nephews, great grandnieces and nephews; along with their spouses, and godchildren.

Albertha Sinclair Toppins was born in New Orleans on November 17, 1929, at a hospital affiliated with the railroads, the only place that admitted Black people. Her father, Joseph Sinclair Toppins, was from Woodville, Mississippi, and her mother, Isabelle Robb Toppins, was from New Orleans, Louisiana.

Albertha’s proud parents separated when she was nine, but they continued to encourage, care for, and nurture her. Her father worked as a laborer for the Southern Railroad. Her mother, a domestic worker, taught herself to become a gourmet chef and was her primary influence and staunchest supporter.

Annie Ruth Pinkey was born on February 19, 1934, in Warrenton, North Carolina, to Helen and Eddie Pinkney Sr. She was the eldest of six children. She learned early the values of faith, education, hard work, and perseverance; these are principles that guided her throughout her life.

She left the family farm to attend Shaw University. After a year, she decided to marry Alphonso Alfredo Petrus. Annie Petrus and Alphonso Petrus lived i n Harlem and were blessed with two daughters, Deborah Yvonne and Victoria Ann. The marriage ended and he preceded her in death. Annie devoted herself fully to rearing her daughters with strength, resilience, and unwavering love.
Jerome Wallace was born to Gloria Wallace and Cardinal Wallace in Jamaica on September 21, 1954. Cardinal Wallace was born in Cuba and his mother in Jamaica.
In 1959 the whole family moved to The United States with his siblings Johnny, Charles, Paul and himself at the time. Later on his baby brother Bruce and his baby sister Joan were born in the states.
Jerome started unicycle basketball in the early 1970’s with the King Charles Troop and traveled with Ringling Brothers & Barnum and Baileys Circus for a while.

Marilyn Louise Thompson was born on November 3, 1939, in Hartsville, SC, to the late Wallace and Rachel Wilson. She and her younger brother, the late Charles Franklin Wilson (Sonny), grew up on 117th St., Madison Park Avenue.  She attended public school and studied at Julia Richman to be a dietitian. She met and married the late Murphy Adam Thompson.

Marilyn was raised in church and was a member of the family church, Jordan River Baptist Church, located in New York City. She also previously attended Glendale Baptist Church and First Corinthians Baptist Church.

On a beautiful day in December of 1942, Amos and Mildred Stewart were given a precious gift; a beautiful daughter who they would name Jane. Jane Annette Stewart was born on December 5, 1942 in New York. The oldest of two daughters, Jane spent her early years growing up in a beautiful brownstone in Brooklyn, New York.

The Stewart family later moved to the Bronx, where Jane would spend all of her childhood as well as part of her adulthood. She attended St. Thomas Aquinus Elementary School and Preston High School. Upon graduation from Preston High School, she decided early on to pursue a career in the teaching profession.

Carl Michael Arrington, endearingly known as “Mickey,” entered heaven’s gates from his home on Wednesday, January 28, 2026. He was born in Brooklyn, New York on November 24, 1950, to the late Mr. and Mrs. Wilbur Arrington. He was the second oldest of four children: Late Wilbur (Sparkie); Roslyn (Joy) and Keith.

As a young child, Mickey relocated to the Bronx where he spent his childhood and most of his adulthood. He attended grade schools near his home in Bronx River. He went to James Monroe High School where he was known for his skills on the basketball court.

Eugene (“Gene”) L. Armstrong was born in the Bronx, New York on 01 April 1945, to Neville L. and Rita E. Blackman Armstrong.  He was the younger of two children, his sister being Yvonne W. Armstrong.  Gene grew up with his family in an apartment on Union Avenue before his parents became homeowners in 1951 on Findlay Avenue, also in the Bronx.  After about a decade, he moved with his parents to their next home, further north in the Bronx.  For a time, he lived in an apartment at the Fort Independence area of the Bronx, but later returned to his parents’ home.
Alma Ruth Moore was born on December 1, 1939, in Fountain, North Carolina. She was the third of five children born to Reverend William Benjamin Moore and Lillian Gertrude Johnson Moore.

Alma received her formal education in the public school system of North Carolina, where she attended H.B. Sugg High School. Following graduation, she relocated to New York City, where she began her professional journey as a nurse’s aide at St. Luke’s Woman’s Hospital, providing compassionate care to patients.

Arthurie Dolores Brown affectionately called "La" was born October 16, 1941 in Charleston, South Carolina to the late Samuel and Carolyn Brown. She was moved to Harlem New York at an early age and then to the brand new Wald Houses of the Lower East Side where she has lived until her passing Tuesday, January 21, 2026, while at home surrounded by family.

Dolores was known for her nurturing heart, unwavering kindness, and dedication to her family. A proud graduate of Fashion Industry High School, she dedicated the first chapter of her adult life t o her greatest passion sewing.

Bernice Wyatt was born December 17, 1926 in New Orleans, Louisiana, to parents Oscar and Vivian Blache. She and her sister attended St. Mary’s Academy in the French Quarter. She subsequently attended Xavier University of New Orleans, where she majored in music and minored in Math. There she met her future husband, Kelley Wyatt, who became an accomplished vocal coach and accompanist. After college, Bernice spent two years living in Miami, where she worked as a band teacher and led the high school marching band—an uncommon accomplishment for women to do at that time.

Denise Cooper was born on February 10, 1971, to Lucille Cooper and Leslie Matthew Cooper. She began her education at CES 90 Elementary School, then continued to CES 82 Junior High School, and later attended Martin Luther King High School. Denise briefly studied criminal law at John Jay College of Criminal Justice, but her true passion was to become a veterinarian, inspired by her deep love for animals (especially her cats Sparkle, Cinnamon and Pepper) and the unconditional affection they give.
Denise went on to dedicate over twenty-six years of loyal service to Marshalls and TJ Maxx combined where she worked faithfully and diligently until her passing.

Amilcar (A-mil-car)  was born in New York City to Ethel Collins (Charleston, SC) and the late Pois Foray (Sierra Leone, West Africa). His name was chosen by his father who was impressed by the diplomat and political organizer, Amilcar Cabral who hailed from Guinea Bissau, West Africa. Amilcar Cabral was instrumental in liberating his country from the Portuguese and his name symbolizes leadership and strength.

As a young child Amilcar was involved in many activities such as baseball with the Hudson League. At the Harlem School of the Arts, where he studied piano and tap dancing for males, to promote the continuation of the art of tap dance.

Deborah Ann Williams was born in Harlem 71 years ago to Carl and Shirley Williams, and from the very beginning, she came with instructions: don’t play with her and don’t mess with her family. She took no foolishness and lived life boldly, loudly, and on her own terms. Deborah was a force—equal parts laughter, love, perseverance, and fire.
Her humor was unmatched and her laugh unforgettable. She showed love through fried chicken, turnips, and cakes made straight from the heart—and correction through a plastic wiffle bat.
Today, we gather to honor and celebrate the life of Phyllis Diane Lewis-Miles, a remarkable woman whose presence filled every room and whose impact will be felt for generations to come.

Phyllis was born on May 26, 1957, in Mathews, Virginia, to Shirley Peterson and Ivory Lewis. From an early age, she was active, inquisitive, and curious about the world around her. After graduating from Mathews High School, she moved to New York, where she built a life marked by purpose, achievement, and profound influence.

These are just some sentiments used to describe Stephanie Martin, the 2nd born child of Floyd and Dorothy Martin. Born in Harlem on February 25th, 1963, just ten months after her big sister’s birth, it was apparent since childhood that Stephanie would live a life filled with assurance, ardor and achievement.

From K-12 she consistently excelled in school. She was the class president; she won the Honor Roll, and she took advanced course work; and at Martin Luther King Jr. High School, she averaged the 2nd highest GPA of her entire graduating class, crowning her the Salutatorian for the class of 1981.

With heavy hearts, but spirits lifted by cherished memories, we announce the passing of Avis Wray—mother, grandmother, wife, sister, friend, and confidante—who departed this world on December 10, 2025 at Bellevue Hospital in Manhattan, New York.

Avis’s journey began on Spring Bank Road, affectionately known as “big yard,” in the lush parish of Portland, Jamaica. Born to Eulalee Carmenta Passley-Brown and Aubrey Adland Brown, Avis was the beloved sibling of Meritta, Elred, Lawna, Kenny, Grace, Errol, Jess, Aubrey Jr., Webster, David, Wayne, Rohan, Bevene, and Byron.
William Henry Jones  of the Bronx, New York, suddenly passed away on Sunday, November 16, 2025.
William aka Bill was born on December 5th, 1947 and was an only child to his parents.

He attended the NYC school system graduating from Dewitt Clinton HS and furthered his higher learning to attend and graduate from Central State University in Ohio. He ran track for his H.S. and college schools. Whilst at Central State, he was enlisted in the ROTC (Army).

Mildred Evelyn Segee , daughter of Carrie Blair-Marshall and Edward Marshall was born on January 5, 1922. She grew up in Harlem and attended both elementary and junior high school there. Mildred was a graduate of Julia Richmond High School.

In June of 1942, Mildred attended a State Guard function at 369th Regimental Armory and met her beloved William. After a short courtship, William and Mildred were married in December 1942. They loved doing things together and spent 47 years as man and wife. Their only daughter, Veronica, was born in March 1944.

Brenda was the second child born to Vivian Lorraine Shaw Maxwell and Oscar C. Maxwell, Jr. Her father was the pastor of Baptist Temple Church, and her mother, in addition to being a homemaker, was active in many aspects of the church and PTA as well a paraprofessional teacher in the Head Start Program. Brenda attended The Little Red School House in Greenwich Village for elementary school and later the John Peter Tetard Junior High School and Roosevelt High School, both in the Bronx. The family, parents and four children, lived in Harlem on 120th Street until Brenda was 9 years old when they moved to the Bronx.
Sharon Rose Henry Russell was born in St. Ann, Jamaica to parents Gwendolyn Johnson & Oscar Henry on June 28, 1960. She was the sixth of ten children.

Sharon attended Dunrobin Primary School in Kingston, Jamaica then she continued her education at Pembroke High School. After graduating Sharon entered Office Administration. Sharon decided it was time for a relationship and while being in Kingston, Jamaica she met Winston Robinson, the union produced a bouncing, bubbling baby boy, Richard Robinson.
Joseph Guy Eshu Miwa Reece was born on July 26, 1959, to Mari Ann and Edmond Reece in Brooklyn, New York. He began his journey to the land of the Ancestors on October 18, 2025.

Joey’s early years were spent in Brooklyn, NY where he attended Our Lady of Good Counsel, Boys’ High School, and Staten Island Community College. He was an avid and competitive basketball player. Although he was not the tallest on the court, he played with the heart of a giant. While playing the sport he loved, he injured both his knees but that did not stop him.
Gloria Ann Byrd, a cherished matriarch, vibrant soul and devoted educator passed away peacefully leaving a legacy of compassion, wisdom and joy.

Gloria was born in New York City on February 28, 1946. She graduated from the High School of Commerce in June, 1964.  She further earned both a bachelor’s and a master’s degree of Science Education from the City University of New York. For 28 years, she served as a dedicated educator in Harlem Community School District #5 where she cultivated young minds and nurtured hearts.

Shirley Muirhead was born Shirley Eva Carlisle in Harlem, New York, on February 10, 1934. The youngest of Edith and Louis Carlisle’s three children, Shirley was sister to Leonard Carlisle (deceased) and June Crump (deceased), and was lovingly raised by her grandmother Eva Perry, her guardian Ruth Dodd, and a devoted community of family and friends.
Cynthia Ferrell  was born in New York to the proud parents of Samuel and Vivian Ferrell on May 17, 1960. She was the oldest of three children.

Born into a life filled with resilience and compassion, Cynthia lived each day with grace and a genuine love for others. Affectionately known as “Pumpkin,” she carried herself with a warmth and joy that made people feel at home in her presence. She was a devoted Christian woman who placed her faith at the center of her life, always drawing strength and peace from her relationship with God.

With profound sadness we announce the passing of Sandra Burton, affectionately known as “Soni Bird” to her family and childhood friends. Sandra transitioned to eternal rest on September 6, 2025, at the age of 60. She was born on August 10, 1965, at Brooklyn Jewish Hospital in Brooklyn, NY, to the late Christine Harris and Robert Harris.
Sandra was a proud graduate of John Dewey High School in Brooklyn, NY, and later attended Borough of Manhattan Community College.

Wendell Isaac Smith  was born on July 9, 1963, to Isaac Smith Jr. and Mattie Williams Smith in Brooklyn, New York. He was educated in the New York City Public Schools and graduated in 1982 from George Westinghouse Vocational and Technical High School.

To know Wendell was to love him. His gentle spirit, nurturing heart, and quiet strength made everyone feel cared for. Even as a young man, he placed family above all else, setting aside his own social life to work and contribute to his family.

Helen Marie Thompson Davis was born on April 27, 1953, in the Bronx, New York. She was the daughter of Mary Thompson and Alphonse Mills. She was raised in the Patterson Houses of the Mott Haven area of the Bronx and was educated in local schools. Helen attended Fashion Industries High School and later attended Lehman College at City University of New York, where she received a Bachelor of Arts degree.
Pastor Helen met and married Charles Davis in 1972. She was the proud and doting mother of three sons: Jonathan “Hassahn” Davis, Lamene K. Davis, and Keith T. Walker.
Alfonso Fitzgerald Dixon was born on Friday, January 10th, 1964 in the Bronx, New York to Harold Bell and Gwendolyn A.D. Thomas.
Fonzo, as he was affectionately known, worked at Jerry and Ron’s Antique Pieces and Furniture Store at an early age.
He was a caring and loving uncle. He helped and reared many kids, but unfortunately he didn’t have any of his own. If you knew Fonzo all you could do was love.

Beatrice Callie Chambers Brown was born on June 9th, 1950 in Harlem, New York to the late James E. Chambers and Mary Frances Chambers. Beatrice was the fourth child born out of six children and the mother of three boys. She was preceded in death by her husband (Douglas Brown), mother (Mary Chambers), her father (James Chambers), one brother (Ronald Dix), two sisters (Carrie Meacham and Virginia Griffen) and two sons (Darryl and Keith Chambers).
She attended the New York City Public school system and later worked for the New York City Housing Authority.
With heavy hearts, we announce the passing of Norma Gene Walter, affectionately known as Mom, on July 15, 2025. She departed this world peacefully, surrounded by the love of her family.

When you talk about living a full life, it would be impossible not to speak of Mom. Migrating from Jamaica at a young age, Norma faced life’s challenges with strength, faith, and unwavering determination. She worked tirelessly—but never in vain—as she sought to build a better life for her children.
Dearest Mary Bertha,

By My will, you will be born on a beautiful day, July 24, 1929, in a little town on the island of Grenada, West Indies to Sanford and Millicent Alexander. You will spend but a few months in Grenada, after which you will be brought to America. The early days ofyour life will find you attending Saint Mark the Evangelist School, escorted there each day by your devoted sister, Jean. At Saint Mark, you will develop your love of reading, a habit that will last throughout your life.
Denise Ingram was born on August 29, 1953 in New York City to Peggy Joyce Bryan and the late Lee James Ingram Sr.
Niecy, as she was affectionately known to many of us, was raised and attended public school in the Bronx. She moved to Brooklyn in 1971 where she completed her high school education.
Denise’s journey was one of fierce determination and resilience. She enjoyed cooking, attending art museums, opera, ballet, and Broadway shows.

Michael Lorenzo West was born on June 8, 1953, in Beth David Hospital on Manhattan’s Upper East Side to Pearline Godfrey and Abraham Joseph West Michael received a well-rounded education first while attending P.S. 4 in Lower Manhattan, then at P.S. 80 in Italian Harlem. He lived with his mother and his two other brothers, Stephen, the oldest by four years, and Gregory, younger by four years, a fire forced the family to relocate to the South Bronx to a less than friendly environment. Michael, then twelve years old, entered J.H.S. 120 and began to excel in his academic pursuits while constantly getting involved in altercations because he refused to become part of the “norm”. This was a trait that would follow him throughout the remainer of his life.
Second born son, Lorain Avery Jr. became native to Charlotte, North Carolina in the Fall of 1935 to the late Mr.

Lorain Avery Sr. and Mrs. Ora Graham Avery. Lorain Jr. was immediately called and responded to his expected moniker, “Junior”. He was the youngest of four siblings; Johnnie Robert, Celessie, Annie Mae and Pearlee, and they wanted for nothing. He had a normal upbringing: he went to school Monday through Friday, did chores after his homework, and they attended church on Sundays as a family.
Ancil Legall was born on August 2, 1949 to Lenora Conliff and Bertrum Legall at home at 4 Baden Powell Street in Woodbrook, Port of Spain, Trinidad.

He attended the School of Tranquility, where he graduated. He joined a music program when he came to the United States. He then entered into the military on August 21, 1969 and served in Vietnam. He served for two years and was honorably discharged on September 15, 1971.
Ancil met his partner Joy Brown in Flatbush, Brooklyn.

Patricia Cobb, affectionately known as Patty, was born on November 11, 1942, at Harlem Hospital in New York City. She was one of two sets of twins born to Ruth Morris Jackson and Albert “Jackie” Jackson. Arriving just seconds before her beloved twin sister Penelope “Penny” Jackson, Patty was a proud Harlem girl from 120th Street. She grew up surrounded by love, laughter, and a big family, including her siblings Albert Jr., Jewel, Penny, Carolyn, Richard (Dick), Elizabeth (Liz), and Anthony (Tony).
On July 4, 1963, Patty married Major Cobb, together they had three children: Michael, Jewel, and Kevin Cobb. She is now joyfully reunited with her beloved son Kevin.

Eugene, Junior or Gene , was born on July 13th, 1942 to Alice (Simmons) and Eugene Wilson, Sr. in Mount Pleasant, South Carolina. He and his family moved to New York City while he was still an infant.

Gene went through the New York Public School system growing up, graduating from Grace H. Dodge Vocational High School in 1960, where he was recognized as his class’s best athlete. Gene served honorably in the US Army. In 1969 he received an associate’s in applied science from Borough of Manhattan Community College and later a bachelor’s in business administration from Pace University.
Larry Stevens was born at Sydeham Hospital in Harlem, NY to Albert and Ruby Stevens on April 10, 1947. Larry would be the fifth child of the eleven children born of this union.

Larry graduated from Benjamin Franklin High School before enlisting in the Army. Always interested in law enforcement he became a Military Police stationed in Germany. Upon his return to Harlem, NY Larry returned to his alma mater, Benjamin Franklin H.S., as part of the security team. While working security he also worked for USPS at night while he studied for the NYPD exam.

Novella “Ella” Bletcher was born March 27, 1934 in Plymouth, North Carolina. Novella was the only child of Lillian (Freeman) and Johnnie Robbins (both deceased). Novella was named Ella after her maternal grandmother Ella Hall Freeman.
At age 3, Novella’s family became part of “The Great Migration”, journeying from Plymouth, NC to Harlem, NY.
It was in Harlem on 128th St that Novella met her close friends, was baptized, attended Metropolitan Baptist Church, married John Bletcher (deceased) and raised two daughters, Crystal and Jewel.

Doris Jean Dixon-Spencer was born on April 25th, 1954 to Dennis Dixon and Lessie Mae Braswell in Ayden, North Carolina, one of what would be sixteen children. From her youth, she was full of a zest for life and had a passion for both loving and helping others. Community, be it family, friends, or neighbors was the very embodiment of who Doris was.

In her late adolescence, Doris would eventually migrate from North Carolina and settle in the Bronx, New York where she lived with her late sister Louise, and her nieces, Annette and Denise, whom would later in life be more like her own little sisters.

Dorothea Ernestine Phifer was born January 19, 1923, to Christine Patterson and Claude Phifer.  Dorothea, an only child, spent most of her childhood with her grandparents Graham and Lula Patterson, three uncles, and six aunts.  Dorothea, also affectionately called Dot or Dottie, graduated from Davidson High School in North Carolina.  Soon after her graduation, Dorothea moved to New York City which was her home for over eight decades.
Dorothea enjoyed a full life in New York.  She loved the city and never considered living anywhere else.

Monica Ruth Myers transitioned on Monday, March 31, 2025 and she will be dearly missed by her family and friends. Monica (a.k.a., Mookie, Moni, Moni-bear, Chipmunk) will always be remembered as a beautiful soul with a bright spirit. She was someone who lived fully, gave generously, and inspired endlessly. She was a radiant force, a natural-born leader whose brilliance, ambition, and vibrant spirit lit up every room. Eclectic in style and soulful in nature, she carried herself with grace, intelligence, and authenticity. Her presence was both refreshing and commanding, and her essence truly unforgettable.

James M. Grant was born in Thomson, Georgia, to Guy Grant and Gussie Paschal on August 28, 1936. He had one sibling, a sister, Beatrice Grant. Most of his family and friends referred to him as “Jimmy.”

Jimmy moved from Georgia to New York City as a young boy. He attended P.S. 157 on 126th Street and St. Nicholas Avenue and graduated from Brooklyn Automotive High School. Jimmy excelled as a student and as an athlete. He won accolades in track and field and was a lifelong member of the New York Pioneer Running Club. Jimmy was a dutiful son and worked alongside his parents in the family delicatessen.
Eustace Vernon Fenton, the first of eight children of long departed Christopher and Edith Fenton of Salem, Montserrat was born on April 2nd, 1936 and passed into glory on 29th March, 2025.

He attended the Salem Primary School before going on to the Montserrat Grammar School as it was called at that time, which is now called the Montserrat Secondary School. After graduating from school he worked as a cashier at the Peters and Peters’ Drug store before obtaining a government job at the Montserrat treasury department.

Marita Wing  was born in NYC to the proud parents of John and Jessie Wing on March 11, 1941. She was the eldest of seven children. Marita was raised by her aunt and uncle at 1730 Amsterdam Ave, better known as Sugar Hill. She attended P.S. 186 and I.S. 164, then called Stitt. She graduated from Washington Irving High School (all girls) in 1959. In High School she ran track and played on the girl’s basketball team, winning multiple trophies. Three years after High School, she married a kid from the neighborhood named Jimmie Falling in 1962 at New Baptist Church. From that union a son was born named Johnnie.

Catherine M. Morgan  was born in Salem on the beautiful island of Montserrat, West Indies on September 29, 1929. She was the daughter of Albert and Sarah Ann Morgan, the fourth of her mother’s children.

Catherine continued her education at Salem Elementary School. After graduation, she became a teacher and taught school for a short time, then migrated to England. She worked in England for about five years then migrated to the United States in the 60’s.
Diane Thomas was born in New York City to Sally Jackson and Lawrence Thomas on January 19, 1952. She was the sixth of eight children.

Diane was raised in NYC where she attended both elementary and middle school. Her family then uprooted to Jacksonville, FL where she attended William M. Raines High School and graduated in 1970. She then moved to Tallahassee, FL to attend the illustrious Florida Agricultural & Mechanical University, officially known as FAMU (go rattlers!) to study at the School of Education.

It is with profound sadness that we announce the passing of Messiah Z. Nantwi, who was born on March 8, 2002, and left this world unexpectedly on March 1, 2025. Messiah was a beloved son, cherished brother, and a brilliant young mind who touched the lives of many.

He is survived by his devoted father, Patterson, and his loving mother, Leslie. Messiah was preceded in death by his beloved sister Ahjani Akira Nantwi, who passed away two years ago, leaving a void in the hearts of those who knew them both.

Delores Marie White was graciously gifted by God on January 8, 1942. Delores, the youngest of six children, was born in Pittsburgh, PA to parents Ms. Willie Lou Prophet and Mr. Willie Benjamin White. At the very early age of two years old, both of Delores’ parents passed away suddenly due to Tuberculosis. No longer having the care and guidance of her loving parents she was raised by her paternal grandmother, Ms. Sally Shavers in Milwaukee, Wisconsin.
She attended Fourth Street Elementary School as well as Lee Elementary School.

Mrs. Lillian Mae (Burton) Cain  was born in Gumberry, North Carolina on May 6, 1928. She was the 2nd of three children born to the late Paul Burton and Eunice Kee. Gumberry, North Carolina was where she met and married her first husband Chauncey Belle at a very young age and bore two sons, Burton Richard Belle and John Paul Belle.

Lillian was a woman of remarkable strength and determination. Living life on her own terms. She was known for her no-nonsense attitude and straightforward approach to life, qualities that endeared her to many.

Claude Brewer Peterson was a loving husband, father, grandfather, brother, uncle and cousin. A self-made man, he worked tirelessly to put himself through college, ultimately becoming a research chemist who shied away from recognition but loved his work and being in the lab. Passionate about advancing science, he created three patents with the U.S. Patent and Trade Office, while also authoring academic articles based on his discoveries.
Born to Evelyn and Roland Peterson on May 27, 1939, at Harlem Hospital in New York City Claude married and raised two sons, Keith and Dwight.

You may have known him as that smart, knowledgeable and engaging CEO of Binding Products, Inc., a successful business where customers came first and who deeply cared about the awesome staff who worked for him.  Or, maybe you remember that nice man who was a volunteer coach for a little league basketball team.  Maybe you were a neighbor, friend or coworker whose heart was warmed as Freddie proudly and lovingly shared stories about his beautiful children. Our family knows him by his broad smile, deep insights, great sense of humor; and as a loving father, son, brother and friend.
Neil Cedric Dingle was born on August 2, 1948 to Kermit Theodore Dingle and Vivian Barry Dingle in Harlem Hospital in Manhattan, but was raised in The Bronx.

Growing up, Neil was very athletic. He was very good at whatever sport he was competing in, especially basketball, handball, and paddleball. He was also in a bowling league for ten years. He was a very pleasant person to be around with a good sense of humor.
After graduating from William Howard Taft High School, he enlisted in the United States Air Force in 1966.

Wayne Anthony Williams was born on May 3, 1958 to the late Sylvia Williams and Willie Govan. Wayne was the middle child of 3 boys. He was raised with his brothers in Bamberg, South Carolina until the age of seven when his mother relocated him and his two brothers to New York City in 1966.

Wayne completed his education in the New York Public School System. After High School, Wayne served in the US Army for a short time. Wayne was a jack of all trades who worked various jobs to provide for his family and help others. Wayne met Karen Smith in 1990.
For he was
An immovable object—committed, principled, and chiseled by life’s lessons.
And just as well, an unstoppable force—unrelenting, fearless, and imbued with relentless vigor.

Calculated yet unbounded; He stood as a pillar of authenticity. He retained complete faith in his internal worth. We hope he now sees that he is also worthy of rest because his legacy is imprinted on everyone gathered in this room today.
Bettie Ruth Ward was born in Mississippi on September 15th to the late Edith Gill and Jeff Darby. At a young age Bettie accepted Christ as her personal Lord and Savior.
As a young woman, Bettie met Jeffrey Ward and they married on November 29, 1953.
Bettie worked as a dietary aide at Jacoby Medical Center. After 30 years of faithful service she retired.
Bettie leaves to cherish her memories: her children, sister-in-law, nieces, nephews, grandchildren, and a host of other relatives and friends.

YVONNE ELAINE DIXON was the tenth and youngest child born to Madge and William Dicks. She was born on December 22, 1943 in the village of Harlem, New York. All of her nine siblings preceded her in death when she left this earthly life on Tuesday, January 28, 2025 at the age of 81.
Yvonne attended elementary and junior high schools in Manhattan, and graduated from Jane Adams Vocational High School in the Bronx.

Pamela Conner, age 52, passed away peacefully on Wednesday, January 22, 2025 at Calvary Hospital surrounded by loved ones. Pamela was born on January 16, 1973 in Bronx, New York to the late Hannah Toney and Walter Conner. She was the youngest of their five children.

Pamela spent most her life in the Bronx where she planted roots, formed bonds and developed lifelong friendships. She attended Roosevelt High School in the Bronx, and later went on to pursue both a degree in Computer Science and Criminal Justice.

Helen Elizabeth Johnson, lovingly known as “Big Mama,” was born on August 15, 1964, in Harlem, New York, to her proud parents, James Abel and Dolores Larcus. The youngest of six children, Helen carried a bright spirit and a heart full of love throughout her life.

Helen’s educational journey began at P.S. 46, followed by I.S. 10 for middle school, and she later graduated from Martin Luther King High School. Her passion for learning led her to Touro College, where she earned her Associate’s degree in 1999. Determined to further her education, she went on to achieve her Bachelor’s degree in Human Services in 2001.

Joan Deloris (Lewis) Thomas born July 19, 1933 to Clifton Lawrence Sr. and Matoka Lewis in Marion County, South Carolina.  The family then migrated to NYC where Clifton Lewis II (Junior) was born. They settled in Harlem (Sugar Hill).  Joan attended public schools, graduated from George Washington HS then shortly attended college in Virginia. During her formative years Joan enjoyed life to the fullest – being with her friends, enjoying people and having a good time. An “uptown girl” who truly loved her home town, Harlem, and represented a time of Renaissance where Harlem was a place of sophistication, style, grace and Black pride. She loved her community.

Steven Frank Bailey: Born to Blanche Beatrice Bailey and Louis Bailey, at Lincoln Hospital, Bronx, New York, on April 5, 1946. The third child, and sibling to Michael Louis Bailey, and Jacqueline Mary Bailey. Later, there was another addition to the family, Stephanie.

Steven, a Bronx native who attended both elementary and high school in the borough, enlisted in the Marine Corps at the age of 17. This decision sparked a conflict with his mother, who strongly opposed his choice. His father, however, supported his ambition.

Gloria Princella Blanchard was born in New York City, to the proud parents of Edgar Stover and Princella Phillips on October 13th, 1943. At 81 years old, she was the youngest of their two children. After high school, she dedicated her career to the New York City Blood Center as a technician. She was a faithful and long-term member of St. Charles Church and a proud member of the Order of the Eastern Star.
She leaves to mourn her passing: her brother Winfred Phillips and beloved sister Debra (Kim), and her children Princella, Milton, Dorlisa (Calvin Palmer), Michael (Sheila Stover), & Bryette.

Yvonne Eva Smith, born Eva Yvonne Nelson on July 18, 1944 in New York City to Dorothy Miller and Henry Nelson. Yvonne graduated from Central Commercial High School in 1962 where she majored in Merchandising in Midtown Manhattan.
On June 15, 1966, she married Larry Smith and the following November 27th , they welcomed their daughter Brandi Belinda Smith into the world.
Yvonne worked at the Post Office in her early 20’s and then went on to work for the Internal Revenue Service where she retired.

We gather here today to celebrate the life of Bernard Eric Hewitt, Son of Andrea Johnson and the late Garfield Bernard. Bernard was a man whose light brightened the lives of everyone who knew him. Bernard was born on August 8, 1995, in Manhattan, at New York Presbyterian Hospital. the vibrant heart of the city, attending Public School 28, I.S. 164, and Brandeis High School in Manhattan. Bernard’s dedication to learning led him to Bronx Community College, where he earned a degree in Business Administration and Social Work.
Our beloved Father, Husband, Grandfather, Great-Grandfather, Brother, Uncle and Friend was called home on Thursday, December 26, 2024.

He was born to the late Manuel Aviles Ortiz and Monserrate Aponte De Aviles in Coamo, Puerto Rico, USA. He was the middle eldest of 11 children. He worked at a private school, Ethical Culture Fieldston School in Manhattan, as a maintenance worker. Manuel Calixto was very active in doing community work and volunteered his services. He earned the respect of every one in our community. In his late 50s, a brave accomplishment, he went back to school to earn his GED.

Stephanie Anita Dodds was born on May 7, 1948 to Doris Beckman Dodds and Thomas Jefferson Dodds. She passed on December 20, 2024. She had 5 siblings, Roxanne Dodds, Erica A. Dodds and Donna M. Dodds. Her brothers David Dodds and Thomas Dodds, Jr. preceded her in death. Stephanie graduated from Brandeis  High School. She worked as a Nurse's Assistant at the Flower Fifth Avenue Hospital for a few years. Later she was employed at the prestigious law firms of F. Lee Bailey and Aaron J. Broder, where she was an office manager and deposition clerk. Always studious, and driven, she graduated from the College of New Rochelle Rosa Parks Campus, on May 29, 1994, where she received her bachelor's degree

Barbara Alston Fuller, born at Harlem Hospital to parents Nathaniel “Nat” Fuller and Dorothy Louise Alston, grew to become a performer whose artistic career panned Broadway, television, and film. She left an indelible mark on the entertainment industry and the hearts of those she loved. Her journey, marked by resilience, creativity, and compassion, was extraordinary both on and off the stage.
Barbara’s life in show business was remarkable. Barbara also appeared in the play The Wedding Band (1972), a powerful work that explored relationships and human connection.

Devout Christian, Loving Mother, and Loyal Friend, Shirley J. Woods, God’s gift, was born in Sarasota, Florida, on May 30, 1941, to the late Leroy Woods and Mabel McElvy. Up to the age of 14, she was raised by her maternal grandparents, King & Nettie McElvy.

In 1955, Shirley accompanied her mother when she relocated from Quincy, FL. to Harlem NY, in pursuit of new opportunities. She achieved a personal milestone by completing her high school education, a testament to her resilience and commitment to self-improvement.

Garnett Sylvester Lewis was born in Jamaica, WI, and raised in Bellas Gate, St. Catherine on August 3, 1945. Jeremiah 1:5 states “before he was formed in his mother’s womb God knew him and called him to be.” This comforts us to know he is God’s. He was the third of eight children born to Naomi and Henry Lewis. While in Bellas Gate he met his beloved wife Iris Blake-Lewis and together they have five beautiful children Devon Lewis, Marcia Lewis, Wayne Lewis, Jacqueline Lewis, Nadene Lewis. They both migrated to America for a better life for their family. They settled in New York City in the late 70’s, in the borough of Manhattan where he resided until his passing.

Esther "Pate” Middleton graced her parents Osborne and Ethel Hicks, and the world, with her presence on February 1, 1942, in Alexander City, Alabama. Esther peacefully chose to rest in her longtime home of Harlem, New York on December 5, 2024.

Pate, as she was affectionately called, was united in holy matrimony with the late Clinton Maynard Middleton. Upon migrating from Alabama, she found success in New York City through 30 years of employment within the telephone company Bell Atlantic, known more recently as Verizon. She was a devoted mother, sister, friend, and longtime member of Union Baptist Church as an Auxiliary Usher.

Lincoln Beresford Harris was born on August 30, 1951, to the happy parents who preceded him, Beresford, and Joyce Harris, of Eden Vale, St. James, Jamaica. He was the sixth of thirteen children; two younger brothers preceded him. God called Lincoln home on Monday, November 11, 2024.

His education began at Goodwill Elementary School, then went on to Harrison Memorial High School in Montego Bay, Jamaica. Lincoln was an excellent student and excelled in academics which led him upon graduation to work in the Hotel Industry.
We gather at the Well to bear witness to the elevation of the beloved spirit we called SILVENA.
Silvena Sylvia Thomas left this earthly life on Monday, October 14, 2024 at the age of 97.

Born in the St. Catherine parish of Jamaica, West Indies to parents Edwin Thomas and Matilda Brown; Silvena grew-up in the Swamp Lane community of Bog Walk Township. She was the youngest daughter and had 8 siblings: George, Helma, Uriel “Boy Right”, Estella “Moma”, Isaiah “Son”, Lucille, Wilfred “Lynn”, and Velus “Connie”.

Juanita Clayton was born on January 27, 1927, in Wilmington, N.C., to Floria Cooper and Willie James. She was the oldest of 5 siblings. After graduating from school in Wilmington, N.C., she moved to New York City.

Juanita was married twice but had no children from either of these unions. Later in life, she took in and adopted 3 young children, 2 of her great-nephews, and a great niece. (Tyrone Clayton, Jonathan Clayton and Lynette Clayton)
Nathaniel Alonzo Mitchiner, Sr. (Nate) was the welcomed eighth child born to the late Mary Catherine and Albert Samuel Mitchiner.
Nate was raised in a Christian home. He was a member of the Mother A.M.E. Zion Church. He attended Sunday School, Junior Church, Daily Vacation Bible School, Boy Scouts, and Senior Church.

Nate graduated from Theodore Roosevelt High School in 1968. He successfully completed numerous college credits and became a publisher of a problem solving mathematical book for parents, teachers, and students.

Bessie Brewington was born in Camden, South Carolina, the child of Florie Truesdale and John Brevard. She had two brothers John Brevard (deceased) and Robert Truesdale (deceased). Bessie attended Jackson High School and was a member of St. Paul United Methodist Church of Knights Hill Road in Camden, S.C.

Bessie was very proud and always shared with her family about the times she worked on destroyer ships as a welder. We sat in admiration as she shared that with her small body build, they would utilize her to climb into small spaces to fix and weld the ships.

Tavaryl Jerren Ramsey, affectionately known as “Bean”, was born December 31, 1981, in Brooklyn, NY to parents, George Marvin Ramsey and Kathleen Forbes Ramsey. Tavaryl was born and raised in Brooklyn, NY and then relocated to Manhattan, Washington Heights, and later Harlem – where he became a Harlem Nite!
He attended schools in the NYC Public School System - PS145M, Crossroads JHS and Coalition HS. Tavaryl was involved in many sports, including Little League Baseball, Football, and Basketball.
It is with a heavy heart that we share the departure of our dear mother Anne Camila Riclès Larrieux, who joined the stars on October 21, 2024.
Loved by all, Aunt Came leaves behind a legacy of warm memories. Her bright smile and unwavering love for her family will forever be remembered.

Ludwic Clinton Brown, whose personal preference is to be referred to as Clinton, or in Harlem, Junior, was born on August 12, 1943 in the Village of Harlem to Ludwic W. Brown and Leila Evelyn Snowden Brown. He was the fifth of this couple’s six children.

He, like his siblings, was a deeply rooted New York City youngster who was raised in a brownstone (better known as 240) on a tree-lined street that bordered the famous Sugar Hill area and where the “stoop” was transformed into the convention center – winter, spring, summer and fall.

This is the story of Patricia Pressley Johnson. Patricia was a proud, stylish, generous woman that was deeply loved. Called Pat or PJ, she possessed a unique personality. It made her a standout partner, mother, daughter, grandmother and friend. Her trend setting style made her a sought after fashion advisor, venue planner, cook, and business woman. For these reasons, Pat will be missed, remembered and always cherished.
Patricia Johnson was born, Patricia Pressley on May 26, 1951 in New York City.

Marlene Bernice (Biddle) Perrineau was the only child born to Martel Charles Biddle and Elsie Hinson on July 5, 1944, in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. The family eventually moved to Harlem, New York where Marlene grew up and attended Junior High School 164 and graduated in 1958. She then attended The High School of Commerce and graduated in 1962. Throughout her childhood, she met what would become her lifelong friend group (and party cohorts!) - Cheryl Robertson, Beverly Stewart, Alan Williams, Lillian Watkins, Diane Scott, Jo Ann Harris, and Doris Knowles. The group later became known as the “Golden Friends”.

Butler Banks Dowery, a dedicated educator, mentor, and community leader, passed away on September 24, 2024. Born in Shelbyville, Kentucky, on June 25, 1933, he was the second-born son and youngest of three children of the late Robert L. Dowery, Sr., and Malinda Butler Dowery. Butler followed the academic and civic legacy of his parents—his mother, a teacher, and his father, a school principal noted in Who’s Who in Colored America, 1933-37 and Notable Kentucky African Americans.
Butler’s educational journey began in Kentucky.

It is with deep sorrow that we announce the passing of Arthur H. Campbell, age 71, on October 7, 2024. Born in Jamaica, West Indies, on November 23, 1952, Arthur moved to the U.S. as an infant and became a U.S. citizen in 1961. He grew up in Staten Island, New York, where he attended elementary through high school, and ultimately received his High School Equivalency Diploma from New York State.
Arthur was a member of the Lord Teach Me ministry. He was also a devoted supporter and contributor to a God-given fellowship for 27 years, amassing friends in countries throughout the world.

Dorothy Mae Toliver was daughter of the late Cleopatra and James Andrew Toliver Jr., was born April 12, 1947 in Harlem Hospital, New York City. She was named after her mother’s long time friend and beautician. She was the third of four children.

Dorothy was delivered from all her earthly woes, no more pain and suffering on October 3, 2024.  As a teenager Dorothy accepted Jesus Christ into her life and joined Second Southern Baptist Church in the Bronx. She loved singing in the choir with her two sisters praising Jesus for his many blessings.

Kamila Morzy-Harris was born in Gołdap, Poland, to the loving parents Jacek and Halina Morzy on September 27th, 1979. She moved to the United States in her early 20s and built a beautiful life, filled with purpose and care.

Kamila was a devoted wife to her husband, James, whom she met in October 2014. They shared nearly ten wonderful years together and were married in 2017, building a life rooted in love, compassion, and mutual respect. Kamila dedicated her life to helping and caring for children, working as a Behavioral Analyst and touching countless young lives with her gentle heart and unwavering commitment.
Doris Goodwin was born on April 30, 1931 in Charleston, South Carolina to Earnest and Lillian Delyons.

She married James Goodwin, together they left South Carolina and made a life for themselves in New York City. They eventually settled in Harlem, where they lived in Abraham Lincoln Houses for almost seventy years. Doris dedicated her life to raising her children as well as her grandchildren and was a source of strength and inspiration to all who knew her.

Erma Lucille Meadows Malloy, EdD, the youngest of four children to the late Warner E. and Cecile Billups Meadows, was born on March 28th, 1938, in Birmingham, Alabama. She passed to eternal rest on Thursday, September 19, 2024.

Erma attended public school in Birmingham Alabama, graduating from Ullman High school in 1955. She entered Fisk University in Nashville, Tennessee and was awarded a Bachelor of Arts in Biology in 1959.

Carlos Martinez came into the world on July 3rd, 1947, in Puerto Rico. He was the younger of two boys. Soon after, his parents moved to New York City. They moved to the Washington Heights area of Manhattan where Carlos lived the rest of his life. He was very active, and well regarded in his community.

When we were children there were 4th of July fireworks across the river on the New Jersey Palisades. We thought they were in celebration of Carlos’ birthday. We would congregate on Riverside Drive to watch.

Kathleen Lorraine Rosario, widely known and loved as Kath, Kathy, and K.K., passed away on September 3, 2024, at the age of 82, in Clarksburg, Maryland. She was born in Harlem, New York City on July 10, 1942. Kathleen's journey through life was marked by her resilience and determination. Kathleen graduated from Central Commercial High School and furthered her education at Bronx Community College. She built a notable career as a paralegal at District Council 37, where her intelligence and creativity were highly valued.
Sheila Marie Brown was born on April 25, 1950 in Harlem. She was the daughter of the late Eddie Lee Brown and Joan Elizabeth Stone.

At the tender age of one, she was taken in by her beloved grandmother who resided and raised her in Bluefield, WV.  After the first 13 years of her life she moved back to New York City to be with her mother and family. Sheila loved living in NYC. She attended and graduated from Louis D. Brandeis H.S. and received her high school diploma.

Debra Marella Garcia Young, better known as "Cool Deb," passed away o n August 29, 2024, surrounded by her loved ones. She was born in Port of Spain,Trinidad and Tobago, on January 7, 1959, to Sylvia Garcia and Irvin Austin Primus. She is survived by her four siblings: Trevor (Sherrie), Ian, Lisa (Wayne), and Jillian.

She grew up in lunapuna, Irinidad, where she was often seen with her skirt tucked under her belly, shoelaces untied, and herhair in two plaited braids because she had a lot. Every morning, Deb and her aunt would raid the plum tree on their walk to school.

On July 24, 1944 in the U.S. Virgin Island, Ferdinand Victor Hunt was born to the proud parents Evariste Richard Hunt from St. Martin and Daisy Viola Jackson from St. John Virgin Islands. Affectionately known to everyone as “Frenchie” but also called Richard by family and friends.

He has a host of brothers & sisters: Desmond Hunt, Mercedes Hodge (deceased) Joyce Rodriguez, Raymond Groeneveldt, Arthur Wenner (deceased), Warren Petty (deceased), Felicia Hunt (deceased), Annette Petty-Pickering, Janeice Hunt, and Brian Hunt.

Gladys Edwards was born May 8th, 1927, to Elma McIntyre and Ludwig Weir in New York City. Growing up in Harlem, she attended and graduated from grades P.S. 157 and junior high school 129. She also attended and graduated from George Washington High School. Gladys’s Favorite subject in school was biology, and she also enjoyed typing. During that time, she met her future husband, who had enlisted in World War II. In May of 1946, Emmett Edwards and Gladys Weir were married. Emmett worked as a welder, and Gladys worked as a typist for a telephone company. In December 1955, Gladys and Emmett welcomed their son Bruce Edwards into the world.

Hattie was born on Feb 15, 1949, in Charleston, South Carolina to Peter Turner Sr. and Elizabeth Myers Rainey. She attended Jennie Moore Elementary and Laing High Schools in the Town of Mt. Pleasant, South Carolina.

Hattie arrived in New York City in 1967 at the age of 18, with the desire to pursue a new life. In 1969 she met and married Johnny Gardner, a young man from North Carolina. They lived in the communities of both Harlem and The Bronx, New York.

Diane E. McCants, a native of Harlem, New York, was a remarkable woman whose life was characterized by resilience, love, and aspirited personality. Born to Daisy Tillman (deceased) and Phillip Shaw, Diane grew up in the George Washington Carver Houses in Manhattan. She cherished the vibrant community, often spending time outside with friends and enjoying life's moments. Known as “Pugg” for her street smarts and a direct, tough demeanor that belied her loving heart, Diane's early years were filled with strength andcompassion. During this time, she met her childhood sweetheart, M. Anthony McCants.

I, Norman Naazir Person, was born on December 31, 1948 at Harlem Hospital located on 137th Street and Lenox Avenue. My childhood home was just 20 blocks from my birthplace at 68 W. 116th Street, where I lived with my parents, Floried and Oliver Person, the matriarch of the family my grandmother Mama Hughes, my brothers Ronald and Everett, Uncle Bud, and our pet German Shepherd. It was in this vibrant Harlem community that my love for music took root. I dedicated my life to the pursuit of music and to nurturing friendships that became my extended family.

William “Bill” Aiken was born on March 11, 1934 in Harlem, New York to his parents, Eugene Aiken, Sr. and Ida Lee Aiken (née Brown). Bill’s parents migrated to New York from South Carolina in the 1920s, along with other African Americans seeking better lives than they had under the Jim Crow laws in the South. His mother was a presser in the Harlem garment industry. His father had a dream of becoming an electrical engineer which was stifled by his denial of entry into the electricians’ union due to the racial discrimination, leaving his father to ‘fire up’ huge boilers in a laundry mat instead.

On Monday, July 29, 2024, Victoria Gomez Alexander (aka Vickie) joined the Lord and passed away in her home at the age of 89 years after a courageous year-long battle with ovarian cancer. Vickie was born on July 3, 1935, in the Cedar Manor neighborhood of Jamaica, Queens, New York, NY. She was the first of three children born to the late Miguel N. Gomez and the late Edna Trotman Gomez, both Caribbean immigrants from Curaçao and Barbados, respectively. She grew up in Jamaica, Queens, in humble but loving conditions with her parents, her brother, the late Arnold “Mike” Gomez, and her sister, Florence Gomez Clark.

Dr. Carol L. Matthew passed away peacefully on July 19, 2024, in Atlanta. The family matriarch was born on January 17, 1932, in Baltimore, Maryland. She was the second child of Dr. Edward S. Lewis and Mary M. Lewis. Her father, an Urban League executive, moved the family from Morgan Park Maryland to Harlem, New York. Carol attended Music and Art High School and earned a B.A in Child Study at Sarah Lawrence College. She began her master’s degree in social work at Columbia University and completed her MSW at Simmons College, in Boston.

In loving memory of Annie R Wilson, a dedicated professional, cherished mother, grandmother, mother-in-law, aunt, cousin and beloved friend. Annie R. Wilson passed away peacefully on July 9th, 2024, at the age of ninety-eight.

Born on July 31st, 1925, in Spartanburg, South Carolina. Annie R. Wilson was the daughter of Lula Austin and Robert C. Hancock. She pursued her passion for science as a 1947 graduate of North Carolina A&T College with a Bachelor of Sciences degree in biological sciences and graduate studies at NYU in biological sciences.
Our beloved Shavon (“Shavony”) Evelyn Skinner, passed away from this life on July 7th, 2024. She was born to late parents Ora Deborah Stewart and Bernard Skinner on January 14th, 1980.
She is preceded in death by Ora Deborah Stewart (Mother), Bernard Skinner (Father), Evelyn Stewart (Grandmother), Joseph Stewart Sr. (Grandfather), and Cynthia Stewart (Aunt).

Lonnie Charles Early was born in Leland, Mississippi to John and Sarah Early on August 7th, 1933. He was the fifth-born child of eight children – (Deceased) Elizabeth Early, Alex Early, John Early Jr., Elnora Riddle, Willie Mae Belcher. (Living) William Early and Betty Hill.

In 1944, he was 11 years old when the Early family moved to Fort Wayne, Indiana from Mississippi. Lonnie attended and graduated from Fort Wayne Central High School. In 1952, he was drafted into the United States Army and fought in the Korean War, serving until 1955.
Mary Anna Cook was born on December 2, 1944, in Jefferson County, Birmingham, AL. She was educated in Birmingham, AL public schools and continued her education in New York.

Mary received her 2 year degree in communication in NYC. She was employed for 32 years by the Verizon Phone Company. She received many awards and certificates from this job for being a leader and doing her job well.

Mabel Betsy Kirkland, one of 14 children, was born on August 5, 1923, to Frank and Elizabeth Kirkland on Edisto Island, SC, where she spent her early years. She migrated to New York City with her family at a young age.

Mabel devoted herself to raising her two sons as a stay-at-home mom before entering the workforce. She served as a Cafeteria Worker at St. Charles Catholic School and later as Head Cook at Resurrection School, both in Harlem, NY. Known for her helpful, giving, and nurturing nature, Mabel left a lasting impression on colleagues and children alike.

Mrs. Trudy Francis was born in Gough, Georgia to proud parents, George and Anlie Gordon on June 18, 1925. She was one of three children. Trudy moved to Harlem, New York and graduated Julia Richman High School.
Trudy met John Francis at the local ice cream parlor. They married in 1948 and from that union came four children: Stephanie Elizabeth, Natalie Agnes, John Anthony, and Leslie Marie.
Laverne Newman McPherson entered into eternal rest on Sunday, June 2, 2024.

She was a smart, beautiful, hard-working, generous soul. She was born in Brassfield, Kentucky on December 20, 1920 to James Milton Newman and Florence Bates Newman. Laverne was raised on the family farm with her two elder sisters, Marguerite Newman-Park (1900-1998) and Pauline Rogers Stephens Newman (1914-1995). Educated in the schools of Brassfield through the eighth grade, Laverne had to leave home to attend Richmond High School in Richmond, Kentucky because there was no high school for African Americans in Brassfield.

Frederick Raymond Barno was born in New York City, Memorial Hospital, on January 9, 1938. He departed this life on May 28, 2024. Frederick Raymond was lovingly raised by his beautiful mom, Freddie Mae B. Phoebe B-S, and Enrique S.

As a Native New Yorker, Frederick grew up in Spanish Harlem and later moved to Harlem and was educated in the New York City Public Schools. He attended PS 157, JHS 43, and George Washington HS. After graduating high school, he attended Columbia University until he met and married Minnie Lillian.
Eva Gibson-Mott was born in New York City on April 26, 1960. She was the youngest of two children to the late Geneva and Pete Gibson and was predeceased by her brother James McDuffie-Gibson (Lefty).

Eva attended Elementary and Junior High school in Harlem and graduated from Louis D. Brandeis High School in 1979. Also in 1979, she welcomed her only son Teddy M. Gibson who predeceased her in December of 2017.

On Saturday, June 1, 2024, the Lord transitioned our dear Amara Darielle Harris to a place of eternal rest. From the moment she came into our lives, Amara filled our hearts with immeasurable love and laughter. With each passing year, she blossomed into a remarkable individual who loved those around her deeply, honestly, and with all her “old” soul could give.
Amara, affectionately known by many names such as Princess, Lady A, Marabell, Fats, Chunky Chi, and Boo-Keesha, was born on June 5, 2013, to Ashley Fantasia Harris and Maurice Rouse, Jr.

Elfredia Faith Ringgold was born Faith Willi Jones to Louis Andrew Jones and Willie Posey Jones in Harlem in 1930. Her father was a New York City Sanitation truck driver. Her mother was a seamstress who became a fashion designer and couturier under her professional name, Madame Willi Posey designing exquisite and original styles for family and friends in the Harlem community. It was only natural that Faith would develop an innovative use of quilting and storytelling to revolutionize the art world and that she would bridge the gap between fine art and craft traditions. As a young child she was always encouraged to aspire to greater heights, and so she did.

Elfredia Mason was born January 23, 1931 in Greensboro North Carolina to the late Mary and Harvey Waddell. She was raised by her loving, caring father after the early passing of her mother. Elfredia was the youngest of six siblings who all preceded her in death.
Elfredia grew up in Greensboro, North Carolina where she attended public school and graduated from James B. Dudley High School in 1949. Following high school, she attended A&T University.

Beverly S. Smith, born to the late Alice Agatha Dickenson, on November 25, 1932, in Brown’s Town, St. Ann, Jamaica, W.I. She attended school in Jamaica, W.I. until she immigrated to the United States in 1944 and continued her education. She was a faithful and dedicated member of the St. Joseph of the Holy Family Church. Beverly had a great love for God and her church. She served her church both spiritually and financially.
Beverly started working for the Social Security Administration in 1954.

Marie Sadila Gabriel, beloved matriarch and devoted homemaker, passed away on May 29, 2024 at her home in Harlem, NYC, surrounded by her loving family. She was born on March 11, 1934 in Artibonte, Haiti to the proud parents Similor and Omilia Dorcilhomme.

As the eldest of 10 siblings, Sadila embraced her role as a keeper and second mother, nurturing her younger brother and sisters with love and affection. Growing up she mastered the art of farming and housework instilling her lifelong commitment to maintaining a spotless home and serving the most delicious meals.

Hazel Marie Stewart-Green was born to the late Joe Nathan Sr. and Ella Dee Stewart on February 13, 1937 in Marion, Alabama. Hazel was the eldest of the couple's two­­ children. Hazel adored her brother, the late Joe Nathan Jr.
Hazel attended Lincoln High School where she obtained her diploma. Soon after graduation, Hazel decided to take on the big city and moved to New York City.
Elius Lamour came into this world on November 11,1932 in the Dominican Republic. He later returned to his parents’ native Country of Haiti, settling in Trou-du-Nord where he went to primary school.
Early in life, he showed great interest in mastering various skills and pursuits. He was foreman at the largest factory in the Northern part of Haiti and became Union president.
